question: Who is the author of the book 'Ladies Coupe'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Anita Nair**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Anita Nair** is the author of the popular novel "**Ladies Coupe**," which was published in the year **2001**.

• The book is a poignant story about the lives of six women who share their experiences while traveling in a ladies-only compartment of an Indian train.

• "**Ladies Coupe**" explores themes of **gender roles, freedom, and societal expectations**, focusing on the struggles of women in patriarchal societies.

• Anita Nair is a renowned Indian author who writes in English and has received critical acclaim for her works, which often delve into human emotions and relationships.

• Her other notable works include "**The Better Man**," "**Cut Like Wound**," and "**Alphabet Soup for Lovers**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **About Anita Nair:**

• Anita Nair was born in **Shoranur, Kerala, India**, and has a degree in English Literature.

• She has received several awards for her literary works, including the **Central Sahitya Akademi Award** and the **Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award**.

• Her writing often portrays the complexities of human relationships and provides deep insights into the cultural and social fabric of India.

• **Overview of "Ladies Coupe":**

• The novel is set in the backdrop of a **train journey** and revolves around the main character, **Akila**, a single woman in her 40s.

• Through the stories of the other women in the coupe, the book addresses issues like **domestic abuse, loneliness, independence, and self-discovery**.

• The book questions whether a woman can live independently without a man, challenging traditional societal norms.

• **Comparison of Other Options:**

• **Leila Seth:** She was the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court in India and the author of books like "**On Balance**" and "**We, The Children of India**," but she did not write "Ladies Coupe."

• **Twinkle Khanna:** Known for her books "**Mrs. Funnybones**" and "**The Legend of Lakshmi Prasad**." She is a celebrated columnist and author, but not the writer of "Ladies Coupe."

• **Nirupama Rao:** She is a former Indian diplomat and has authored books on foreign policy and poetry, but she is not associated with "Ladies Coupe."

• **Importance of "Ladies Coupe":**

• The novel is considered a classic in modern Indian literature for its strong feminist undertones and relatable storytelling.

• It has been translated into **several languages**, making it accessible to a global audience.
